description: Use before implementing anything that might change the bill: "what does adding SMS reminders cost", "before I add this background-job package", "should we swap Postmark for Resend", "what if we reach 50,000 users". Prices the change against the accepted project (id, needs sign-in) or a plan link (share_url, no sign-in): what changes, services added or removed, the cost before and after and the difference, now and at forecast, with the same users, forecast and usage on both sides; free-tier and quota limits; whether it breaks a must-have (a required region, SSO, HIPAA); alternatives using what the project already has (an existing vendor, or running it on existing infrastructure); setup or migration effort as a range; and what is still unknown. Packages are read with detect_stack's rules: an SDK alone never counts as a bill, two packages of one vendor are one service, and development-only or optional packages are not counted as production cost. Reads only: the accepted plan never changes here. To keep the change, call accept_change with accept_with.arguments after the user agrees. Example: {"id":"<project id>","change":{"label":"SMS reminders","add":[{"category":"sms"}]}} or {"id":"…","change":{"dependencies":[{"name":"bullmq"}]}}.

change.description: What would change. Give only what the user proposes.

add.description: Add a category (best vendor picked) or a specific vendor.

dependencies.description: Packages about to be installed (npm, PyPI and so on). scope: development for devDependencies, optional when it may not be used.

label.description: The change in the user's words, e.g. "SMS reminders". Shown back only.

remove.description: Stop using a category or a vendor.

replace.description: Use this vendor for the category instead of the current pick.

capability.description: Capability id from list_capabilities, e.g. auth.saml_sso.

source.description: The PRD sentence this came from.

usage.description: New users or usage the change brings, e.g. {"per_user":{"sms":4}}.

per_user.description: Usage per active user a month, e.g. {"sms": 2, "file_storage_gb": 0.2, "ai_input_ktok": 30}. Replaces the profile and the filled-in defaults for those units; a plan's questions say which unit each answer sets. Units: mau, seat, request_million, bandwidth_gb, db_storage_gb, egress_gb, email, event, error_event, compute_hour, revenue_usd, transaction, ai_input_ktok, ai_output_ktok, kv_read, kv_write, ci_hour, file_storage_gb, file_egress_gb, file_write, file_read, video_min_stored, video_min_delivered, sms, job_run, search_request, search_record.

expected_version.description: The context_version you last read. If the project moved on since, the answer says so and is priced on the current version.

id.description: The saved project (needs sign-in). Its accepted plan is the "before".

share_url.description: A plan link, when there is no saved project (no sign-in). The change can be priced but not accepted.

name: price_change

assumptions.description: Usage and pricing assumptions behind the numbers.

caveats.description: Show to the user word for word.

completeness.description: On plan and project results: complete, complete_with_assumptions, incomplete or needs_clarification, with the reasons. Say plainly when it is not complete.

data.description: The tool result. Its shape depends on the tool.

disclosures.description: Always includes the neutrality note: no vendor pays for a place in the answer. Link its url when you mention how Kong Reviews is paid.

project.description: On results about a saved project: its id and the context version the answer was computed on. Pass both back in follow-up calls.

title: Price a change before building it
